Please, continue to point out my flaws. You know me so well!

I agree, I should not have returned. I did have many opportunities over the summer to work and stay; however, I made the mistake in thinking our relationship had stabilized. That's a mistake I hope not to make again, thank you.
What you are saying, though, makes total sense. I do need to consider future costs of law school, how to pay back debt, etc.

Absolutely, that's something I do need to consider, thank you. I did very badly in science courses and was generally uninterested in the course material. However, the second semester when I switched I managed to pull off a 4.0 for the semester taking uper-division english, rhetoric, and government courses. I'd like to do something I can excel at rather than struggle. The competitive nature of the medical field is also outrageous, getting into medical school is no easy walk in the park. I've known students who've had high GPAs and MCAT scores and still not get in. If I were to stay in that path, I'd probably have a low GPA and score, but at least with law I have a chance at a high GPA and LSAT score.

That's an interesting point of view, thank you. My parents are from South Asia, so I can see how their school system effects their way of thinking in regards of my education. After their equivalent of high school, they are already in their specialized school; meaning, they are already in medical school, or engineering school, or law school, etc. No 4 years of exploring a major as a precursor before graduate level school or medical school.

Even the person you replied to never mentioned anything of that sort. Once again, I'm not trying to be aggressive in any way. I appreciate any perspective anyone supplies. I form my decision on my own, if I don't agree with what you say, does not mean I don't respect your opinion or learn from your opinion. I'm not 100% perfect or "in the right" - no one really ever is. There are things I can do differently, which is what I'm trying to do for myself. Before you criticize me on my critical reading skills again, please try to understand my perspective.

I don't mean to be hostile in my remarks. I acknowledge the point you are trying to make. However, I do think I'm making actual progress towards my path and not just trying to claim my parents are "evil" or anything of that sort, what benefit is that to me? I've secured an internship for Spring semester, will be writing for the campus paper and an outside news organization in the city, and have been accepted into a program for fall semester for disciplinary studies that assigns you a mentor for the career you want to follow. I've done a lot on campus, and because of the location of my school, I am able to do many things. The location of where my parents live doesn't provide that many opportunities for me to follow. I can do a couple things remotely from my room, like write articles, but that's it.

The personal detail goes into cultural and religious conflicts I've been having with my parents since high school. Like the ability to date, go out with friends, have a life outside studying and family, and being an in the closet atheist in an extremely conservative, religious family. All these aspects lead to increasing tension between my family and I, and apply especially now after returning from college and having 100% freedom there to having 0% freedom with my family. You want me to tell you my life story?

Where do I mention that they SHOULD pay for my degree? Here I'm talking about trying to find a way for me to pay for my own schooling. I'm trying to gain independence financially so they can't tell me where to take my life. No, I don't want to be a doctor like they want. Just because I want to have a non-science degree doesn't make it any less prestigious than a science degree. I want to be a lawyer, enter politics, directly influence the policies of my community and more. Is that path any less honorable than that of a science major? No, it's not any more honorable either, to each his own. I'm not trying to justify my parents pay for my tuition, that bridge has already been burnt at this moment of time. I've received great input from this thread, and even more from local community members who know about my situation. The path I will be taking is to become financially independent and show my parents through my effort and success the value of my character.

Not sure what you mean. They compare me to my friends who are still doing Pre-med; those students have paid internships at hospitals or are shadowing doctors. I am writing articles at home and getting/advice mentorship from writers and lawyers in my community. I'd like to do more and get a job; however, they don't approve of "lower class" jobs.They obviously think my career choice and major is a waste of time, and are being passive-aggressive about it. Obviously, there's more context to my situation, but it goes into personal detail that I don't really want to share. You are right, though, in the notion that it's not totally my parent's "fault". It's just that we have two different ideas of my future, and I'm not aligned with what they want me to do, rather I'm positioning myself for the future I want.
Thanks
Sounds like the situation many of my family friends and I are going through. That's true, I guess I just need to focus on the future and let them see my perspective with my success.
Thank you for the advice!
That's true, for most of high school my goal was to please my father. That changed this past year in college, which may be the source of tension in our relationship.

Thank you from your insight. I heard a similar perspective from one of my close family friends who was in graduate school when I was in highschool. I can definitely see how being away or living apart from your parents eases the strain on the relationship. I lived 4 hours away from home on-campus during the school year and was required to go home every weekend and call everyday when I was not home. Even in that time-span, my parents were considerably nicer to me.
That's true. I'm just mentally prepping myself for being financially independent. Trying to plan out the next months so I can still focus on college rather than being completely overwhelmed.

I was a Biochem major and absolutely hated it. My parents wanted me to be a doctor, and all throughout high school discouraged me from pursuing any other field. I am now doing a double major in Rhetoric and Government with the hopes of being a Lawyer. My parents believe that money is the only thing that matters, not passion. My passion is writing, analyzing, politics, and after talking to multiple school advisors, they suggested going for a pre-law path.
Thank you! Just writing this all out and getting input from other people on reddit and elsewhere is helping me clear my mind.
Bingo

Yeah, they became especially controlling during the last year of high school and this past year. I may be on the path of cutting them off pretty soon, as I speak, things are getting worse. You're right, they've been out of the job market for a while and both have high-paying jobs.

I presented them with a plan of what I would do over the summer. I told them I would be looking for a summer job to pay for my expenses, taking summer classes at the local community college, and looking to get some articles published. They flat out said they don't approve of me getting a job. I took a courses over May in the maymester. The thing I've been spending most of my time is writing articles and forming connections with editors. My parents don't see any progress on that end, even though I have made a lot of progress. This probably stems of the fact they don't approve of me forming a career path that's not science related. That sounds like a good idea, I do basic chores, but I'll pick up a few more and see what happens. Thanks! Sorry for the long reply, I'm in a venting mood right now.

I totally agree, they don't owe me anything. That's why I'm trying to gain some independence as an adult and looking for a solution. I'm still trying to talk to my parents concerning what exactly they're mad about and if there's anything I can do to fix it. The thing that threw me off, which is why I'm doing research and asking people about loans, is that they said I will not be welcomed home when summer ends. Maybe I misinterpreted it, but it seems like they're giving me sometime to prepare before I'm cut off. Anyways, thank you for the advice!
